correspondence.component_scope: western opening and first lake approach
correspondence.finding: The chosen western opening follows a shallow eastward tundra drainage trough with small ponds and a narrow winding stream corridor. Its northeastward approach reaches the southwestern arm of the first irregular lake. Neighboring parallel bedrock depressions are visible, but the selected opening and this lake approach are geographically coherent at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: first irregular lake and northeastern transfer
correspondence.finding: The selection crosses an irregular lake and follows its eastern-to-northeastern pond-and-stream trough. The inspected upper detail shows the adjoining low wet corridor and small intervening waterbodies continuing toward the western end of the next elongated lake system. This is an ordinary lake/stream connection, without asserting precise present flow direction or a continuously wet thread at every point.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: upper ribbon lake and broad eastern basin
correspondence.finding: A long narrow bedrock lake complex, with several parallel arms and connected wider eastern water, occupies the selected middle corridor. The chosen parts correspond to this lake system at useful geographic scale; its separate arms are not independently named in the material.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: lake to northern feeder transfer
correspondence.finding: The stored selection leaves the northern side of the upper elongated lake region, turns north across dissected rocky upland and proceeds east to a northern tributary trough. The photographed lake has a clear eastern connection into a canyon farther south, which reaches the larger east-side receiving valley. The inspected material does not establish a geographic through-link from this lake to the more northerly feeder followed by the selected parts. This is the single material transfer gap; the photograph is not used to repair or reroute the stored selection.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: eastward receiving valley and first lower lake
correspondence.finding: East of the unresolved upper transfer, the selection descends through a visible receiving valley and follows a long downstream lake with multiple islands, narrow arms and an eastern constriction. This portion is geographically supported independently of whether the selected northern transfer actually connects to the earlier lake.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: second lower lake and coastal approach
correspondence.finding: The first long lower lake narrows through the eastern receiving trough into a second elongated lake. Its eastern end feeds a short winding channel across the low coastal margin toward the inlet visible farther east. The ordinary lake-to-stream and coastal-floor correspondence is supported without a present hydraulic-state claim.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: actual source and rendered terminal neighborhoods
correspondence.finding: The last part reaches the low coastal outlet corridor. The stored source endpoint falls in the outlet/foreshore neighborhood beside the channel entering the inlet. The rendered ending lies farther south on the adjacent low coastal margin, near small wet depressions, rather than at the same photographed water point. Both endings were inspected separately and retained; neither was moved onto a preferred channel or treated as a precise current shoreline measurement.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the selected fragment.

Both photographs cover this entire opening and its contiguous basin setting. This is ordinary landscape correspondence, not a claim that every selected segment is a presently wetted channel or that the chosen position is an official river source.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the selected fragment.

The selected path runs through this connected water and its southern basin margin. A substantial adjoining river and small side channels are separately visible to the west; they are not substituted for the selected northward continuation. No lake name was established from an inspected naming source.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward passage beyond the large lake, across ponded wetland and a separate elongated pond/lake, into the northern meandering receiver.

Neither the overview nor the detail establishes an ordinary outflow/receiving connection spanning this whole selected northward passage. Mere proximity of the lakes, ponds and river is insufficient. This is a real missing lake-to-receiver transfer, not a demand for exact bank alignment, a current wet thread or proof of present hydraulic operation.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the selected fragment.

Its western bends, the selected continuation and neighboring lateral wetland channels are visible in both photographs. The selected receiver from this point downstream is geographically supported, but an independently read hydronym for this upstream receiving reach is absent.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestward meanders, western turn and junction with the broad lower river.

The generalized selected segments remain within that ordinary corridor despite shortcutting individual bends. No distinct upper-stream name is inferred from the downstream Black River site label.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Broad lower river, western bends and coastward meandering approach.
correspondence.finding: The lower river is continuously visible from the receiving junction through broad tidal-looking reaches and the final western meanders to its coastal outlet. The independent Western Alaska spill-response workgroup matrix lists Black River at this photographed coastal outlet vicinity. Together these sources support Black River for the bounded lower/coastal receiving corridor, without extending that name to the unestablished lake-to-receiver passage or to every upper component.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the selected fragment.

The rendered endpoint is instead at the coastal margin north of the photographed river mouth; the last display segment crosses the adjacent estuarine plain. Both terminal settings were inspected and kept separate. The rendered extension is not treated as a natural named river channel, a surveyed mouth line or evidence of flow across the intervening plain.

All selected joins remain within this connected valley rather than crossing a separating ridge.

This supports ordinary geographic correspondence without requiring a blue line or current surface flow across every field.

Adjacent small ponds are not treated as required lake-transfer links.

correspondence.finding: The lower selected corridor bends east across the cultivated western receiving plain toward the large lake. correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the selected fragment.

correspondence.finding: The selected route crosses the western margin into the large receiving lake, corresponding to Laguna de Bustillos in the independently read regional basin description. This is a river-to-lake transition; it does not require an inferred transfer to another basin.
correspondence.part_index_basis: One-based stored part numbers within the selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: lake interior extension and actual end
correspondence.finding: The remaining selected parts traverse the lake interior, turn south and southeast, and end within the southern lake area. The complete entry-to-end lake setting is visible; mosaic water appearance does not establish present water level or hydraulic flow.
